title: SR-2.03 Every client hook verified against the real app
request: Closes G23: Codex, Gemini and Windsurf env markers admitted unverified (common.mjs:80); a vendor change silently breaks hooks. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Conformance per client
requirements: for each of 8 clients a recorded fixture of the real hook payload and env, captured from a named app version

for each client, the conformance fixture shows whether the hook's output reaches the model (for Cursor's prompt hook, src/cli/hooks.mjs:45); where it does not, docs/CLIENTS.md says so for that client and event

the 8 clients are claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, cursor, claude-desktop, windsurf, vscode and zed; each fixture names the app, its --version output, captured_at and the capture command, and each hook client has a fixture for every hook event memev registers for it

each env marker in ENV_MARKERS is confirmed by a recorded launch fixture of its app (the env and parent process name the memev mcp process saw), and the running-app markers in src/cli/bus-cli.mjs agree with them; test/helpers/cli.mjs no longer calls any marker unverified
the hook reads each payload field the fixture records (session id, project, prompt) under the app's own field name, never falling back to a default for a field the app sends
the hook registration memev writes (event keys, matcher form, timeout unit, version fields) matches the config the named app version accepts, and the Cursor loop cut-off is read from one place

docs/CLIENTS.md has a 'Hook limits' table whose (client, event) rows are exactly the pairs whose output does not reach the model, and a Supported versions table with one row per client whose version equals its fixture's
npm test runs the conformance suite, and no registered hook event is dropped to avoid recording a limit

criteria.statement: Each client fixture parses and produces context

verifier.cmd: f=$(mktemp) && node --test --test-reporter=tap 'test/clients-conformance/*.test.mjs' > "$f" 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -30 "$f"; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && grep -qx '# skipped 0' "$f" && grep -qx '# todo 0' "$f"

criteria.statement: For every [VAR, client] in ENV_MARKERS imported from src/cli/common.mjs, the client's recorded MCP-server launch fixture (the env and parent process name seen by the `memev mcp` process that the named app version launched) has VAR set to a non-empty value. The fixture's recorded parent process name, normalised as common.mjs:91 does, must not map to another app through PARENT_NAME_AS_APP (common.mjs:90) or KNOWN_APPS (common.mjs:87), so the seat cannot be relabelled at common.mjs:111-113. A marker whose client has no launch fixture fails, and so does a claude-code launch fixture without CLAUDECODE. Do not use an effectiveClient(client, env, 0) equality: with ppid 0 it returns the claim for any env (common.mjs:95,116).

criteria.statement: For each of the 8 clients there is a test named 'SR-2.03 conformance <client>'. It JSON.parses the fixture's recorded stdin itself (not through runHook), then runs `memev hook session-start` with that stdin, env and format against a live sandbox vault (sandbox() + init) whose card holds a seeded sentinel. It asserts that stdout parses in the client's recorded output shape, contains the sentinel, and contains neither 'not reachable' nor 'could not start'. Instructions-mode clients assert the same sentinel in the MCP initialize instructions.

criteria.statement: For each hook client's prompt fixture, the test runs the prompt hook against a sandbox vault seeded with a memory matching the fixture's prompt. It asserts the journal holds a user entry whose text equals the fixture's prompt, under the session id taken from the fixture's own recorded field (session_id or conversation_id, never 'session'), with project equal to the slug of the fixture's cwd or workspace_roots[0]. tasks.title: Scheduled drift check
requirements: a weekly job checks each client's latest release notes and hook schema and opens an issue on change

the drift job runs weekly with issues: write, compares each client's current version and hook schema with the Supported versions table and the task 1 fixtures, opens one issue per changed client, and treats the vendor's text as data it never runs

criteria.statement: Run scripts/clients-drift.mjs --dry-run against a local directory of per-client release-notes and hook-schema snapshots, using the baseline from the docs/CLIENTS.md Supported versions table and the T1 fixtures. With one client's latest version or hook schema changed, stdout JSON lists exactly one open-issue action naming that client and its old and new values. With nothing changed, it lists none. The test also reads the text of .github/workflows/clients-drift.yml and asserts a weekly `schedule` cron, `permissions: issues: write`, and a step that runs `node scripts/clients-drift.mjs`.
